source_title: Eleventh Annual Report of the Trustees of the Peabody Museum of American Archaeology and Ethnology (vol. 2, pp. 339-347, Putnam, 'Archaeological explorations in Tennessee')
author: F. W. Putnam (map from a survey by A. H. Buchanan)

where.page_or_leaf: fold-out map at leaf n356 (between printed pp. 338 and 339); text leaf n357 (p. 339)

caption_or_quote: Map title cartouche: 'Earthwork on the Lindsley Estate near Greenwood Seminary, Lebanon, Tennessee. From a Survey by A. H. Buchanan.' Text: 'an accurate survey of which, reproduced on the accompanying map, I am indebted to Prof. J. H. Buchanan of Lebanon ... Spring Creek ... makes at this place a bend to the eastward ... an earthwork enclosing an area of between ten and eleven acres ... about 900 feet north-south ... 650 feet east-west ... On this southern bluff are six mounds ... situated as shown on the map'
shows: Enclosure embankment and ditch with bastion-like angles and three causeways, Spring Creek bend, large mound A and smaller mounds B etc., six mounds on the southern bluff, sections at bottom of sheet
licence_basis: PD in US: published 1878 (before 1931).
notes: WARNING: the IA (Google) scan at this URL shows the fold-out still FOLDED - only the title strip and one edge are visible; use Thruston 1890 Fig. 3 (reduced copy of this map) or find an unfolded scan (HathiTrust copies of Peabody Reports vol. 2; blocked to curl). Identity: Sellars Farm site (40WI1) was the 'Lindsley Estate' site Putnam dug in 1877, ~3 mi SE of Lebanon on a bend of Spring Creek (Wikipedia/TN state page). Myer 1928 (BAE 41st) also mentions the walled town 'on the Lindsey farm, 4 miles east of Lebanon'. Thomas 1894 describes the same circular work near Lebanon in text only.

source_title: Map of the battlefield of Shiloh (contoured park survey, scale 1:10,560 = 6 in. to 1 mile)
author: anonymous (Shiloh National Military Park survey; reproduced by Photographic Section, Military Information Division, General Staff, U.S. Army)

where.page_or_leaf: single sheet; mounds at grid K-L / 12 (IIIF region 4900,4500,1400,1300 of 6682x9790)

caption_or_quote: LoC notes: 'Anonymous map indicating roads, drainage, fields, woodland, contour lines, and the "boundary line of park." ... Scale 1:10,560.' Stamped: 'Reproduced in Photographic Section, Military Information Division, General Staff.' Viewed: seven mound outlines drawn on the bluff top south of Pittsburg Landing between two ravines, east of the road, with 10-ft contours (300-320 ft) and the river bank.
shows: Contoured topography (10 ft interval) of the whole park; on the river bluff ~1 mile S of Pittsburg Landing: 7 mound symbols (one large closed ring, others smaller) in a cluster, the bluff edge, the two ravines bounding the mound plateau, road, river bank; numbered grid; north arrow
licence_basis: US federal government work (War Department / General Staff reproduction of the Shiloh National Military Park survey); also published c.1920, before 1931.
notes: Mounds are drawn but NOT labelled; identification is by position (bluff south of Pittsburg Landing = Shiloh Indian Mounds, 35.1415 N 88.3209 W). Contours and ravines make this an excellent fit source for LiDAR; scale 1:10,560 so the mound group spans ~80 px at the 1000-px crop shown. LoC date '[1920?]' is a cataloguer guess; the underlying survey is the 1900s park commission map (Atwell Thompson) - not verified.
